Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Partners Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold as it may be audible. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Partners' financial results for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2023. Joining me on the call are Dr. Emily Carter, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Sarah Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Strategy Officer; David Wong, Chief Information Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Human Resources Officer; and Thomas Lee, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Carter.

Dr. Emily Carter:
Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the fourth quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on eight key aspects: the impact of seasonality or external factors like flu season, the impact of value-based care contracts on reimbursement, the impact of acuity mix changes on revenue, initiatives to improve operating margin, trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, capital expenditure guidance for the next quarter and year, same-facility admissions and patient day growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, and the impact of cost reduction initiatives.

Let me start with the impact of seasonality and external factors, particularly the pronounced flu and respiratory virus season this quarter. Winter quarters in our sector are always volatile due to surges in acute care demand, but Q4 was amplified by severe RSV-flu co-circulation, lingering COVID-19 variants like JN.1, and harsh weather in key markets. Across our 52 acute care hospitals and 18 ambulatory surgery centers in 14 states, adjusted patient admissions rose 12% year-over-year to 285,000, driven by a 28% spike in emergency department visits for respiratory illnesses, similar to trends at peers like HCA Healthcare and Tenet. Inpatient days increased 15% to 1.8 million, with our case mix index expanding 4% to 1.72 from higher-acuity cases like pneumonia and sepsis linked to influenza. This varied regionally: our Northeast facilities in New York and Pennsylvania saw 22% admission growth amid CDC FluView positivity rates peaking at 35%, while Sunbelt markets like Texas and Florida grew 8% due to milder weather and tourism volumes.

On revenue, this drove net patient service revenue to $4.2 billion, up 14% year-over-year, with seasonal factors accounting for about 60% of the growth. Medicare fee-for-service benefited from the higher CMI, adding $180 million via IPPS wage index adjustments, though offset somewhat by the 2.7% OPPS update lagging cost inflation. Commercial payer mix stayed at 42%, but better rates on seasonal acuity lifted average revenue per admission 7% to $18,500. Costs rose too: antiviral supplies like Tamiflu and Remdesivir increased 22% to $45 million, and contract labor surged 35% to 18% of nursing payroll in peak weeks, pressuring hospital EBITDA margin to 18.2%, down 110 basis points sequentially but flat year-over-year adjusted. Still, consolidated adjusted EBITDA of $825 million beat guidance by $25 million due to proactive steps.

We've built resilience with our Epic MyChart integration live in 90% of facilities, ramping virtual urgent care 40% during peaks and diverting 15,000 lower-acuity ED cases to save beds. Our FluSmart predictive analytics, partnered with Cerner and Google Cloud using FluSurv-NET and wastewater data, forecasts surges two to three weeks ahead, letting our Workforce Command Center cut overtime 25% and agency rates from 22% to 14%. In Midwest markets, micro-hospitals with Teladoc handled 8% of seasonal volume off-campus. Looking ahead to Q1 2024, CDC flu projections suggest moderate activity with El Niño upside; our $250 million capex includes bed expansions and HVAC for surges, targeting 200 basis points EBITDA margin growth over two years. We've hedged with value-based contracts covering 25% of lives, tying shared savings to readmission reductions. Overall, these factors create lumpiness—like our 22% sequential revenue acceleration—but we manage them to outperform through cycles.

Next, the impact of value-based care contracts on our reimbursement. At year-end, these contracts made up 35% of total net patient revenue, up from 25% in 2022 and 12% in 2020, aligning with CMS pushes via MSSP Track 3 ACOs, BPCI Advanced bundles, and commercial efforts from UnitedHealthcare's Optum and Elevance Health. Across our 42 acute care hospitals and 120 outpatient facilities in 12 states, our shared savings reached $68 million in 2023, up 42% year-over-year net of $12 million downside risk, strong per-bed at $1.2 million versus Tenet's $950,000.

By payer: Medicare at 52% of revenue saw our three NextGen ACOs with 150,000 lives shift to 103.5% of benchmark from 98%, yielding $42 million upside from 15% readmission cuts to 14.2% via CareBridge and Epic Cosmos analytics, plus 95/100 MIPS scores for 5.2% MVV boost. Medicaid at 18% delivered $15 million incentives in VBC-heavy states like California and New York, with 12% diabetes A1C improvements; Southern markets lag at 22% penetration. Commercial at 25% added $11 million from Blue Cross and Cigna bundles in ortho and maternity, at 101% benchmark with 8% lower LOS via ValueSync AI.

VBC adds volatility with 10-15% lower upfront cash, pressuring acute EBITDA 120 basis points to 18.4%, offset by $25 million efficiencies from staffing and Vizient GPO. We avoided $8 million HAC penalties at 96% on PSI-90. Investments include $45 million FY24 capex for digital twins modeling RAF drift, telehealth at 25% of encounters cutting ED visits 22%, and two new MSSP ACOs targeting $100 million savings over three years. Northeast/West Coast to hit 45% VBC share by year-end 2024 versus 28% Sunbelt, with our 4.2 star rating lifting MA revenue 5-7%. We guide 40% VBC revenue in FY24 with $80-90 million savings, mitigated by $120 million 340B optimization against IRA drug costs.

Shifting to the impact of acuity mix changes on revenue, a key driver of our 8.2% growth to $2.85 billion. Acuity mix reflects patient severity via CMI, up 4.1% to 1.87 from 1.80 year-over-year and 1.83 prior quarter. Adjusted admissions rose 5.3% to 142,000, but revenue per admission climbed 2.8% to $19,450, with acuity contributing $185 million or 65% of NOPR growth: volume $72 million, acuity $185 million, payer/pricing $48 million, offset by LOS -$20 million.

Post-COVID elective rebound boosted ortho CMI to 2.45 with 12% hip/knee jumps; medical at 1.65 from sepsis/respiratory. We converted 18% observation to inpatient, adding $12 million. Sunbelt CMI up 5.2% to 1.92 on cardiac/transplants; Midwest 2.8% to 1.78 despite MA downcoding, clawing $8 million via CDI. Our 3M/Nuance CDI and AI advisors queried 42% cases, up from 35%, with hospitalist incentives. Cardio at 28% NOPR with 2.18 CMI, oncology CAR-T over 3.0. Labor up 4.5% pressures margins at 18.2%; payer audits rose. Q4 CMI 1.88-1.90 with flu and $150 million robotics; optimizing via specialists and divestitures for 4-6% 2025 NOPR growth.

On initiatives to improve operating margin, we expanded 180 basis points to 6.8% from 5.0% year-over-year across 28 hospitals and 45 ASCs in Sunbelt markets, third straight sequential gain ahead of 6.5-7.5% full-year guide, targeting 9-10% by 2026 for 15%+ EBITDA growth.

Pillars: Labor (52% costs) down 450 bps via Qventus AI cutting overtime 22%, agency 35%; internal travel at 15% shifts, retention up 12%, $1,620/APD. Supply (22%) improved 220 bps, $150 million savings: Vizient GPO 18-22% discounts, 85% generics, ASC bundles down 14%. Revenue cycle: 97.5% clean claims, DSO 42, RPA cut denials $28 million; commercial 58%. Throughput: ALOS down 6% to 4.6 days, ASC 22% growth at 25% margins, $75 million AI capacity. Sunbelt tailwinds; risks CMS cuts buffered by volume.

Regarding trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, admissions down 2.8% YoY to 112,500, days 1.5% to 675,000 at 6.0 ALOS; outpatient up 6.2% to 1.8 million encounters, 58% EPDs up 3.1%. Same-facility outpatient 7.1%; inpatient surgical -4.2%, ortho flat inpatient but +15% outpatient. Sunbelt +9.4% outpatient; legacy -4.5% inpatient. Payer pushes, $250 million robotics converted 18-22% procedures; 25 de novo ASCs, hospital-at-home 5,000 days. Q4 inpatient mid-single decline offset by 7-9% outpatient for 4-5% EPDs.

For capital expenditure guidance, FY2025 $875-925 million, up 5% from $850 million 2024. Q1 $210-230 million, Q2/Q3 $225-245 million, Q4 $215-235 million. Facilities 42% $370-390M: two 200-bed micro-hospitals Phoenix/Dallas $150M, Midwest renos $100M. Equipment 35% $305-325M: MRIs $120M, da Vinci $80M, Varian. IT 18% $160-165M: Epic $90M, Teladoc $40M. Other 5%. Sunbelt 45%; 15-18% IRR.

Same-facility admissions up 4.8% YoY, 2.1% QoQ to 285,000; days 5.2% YoY, 2.4% QoQ to 1.72 million, ALOS 6.04 days. Access optimization cut no-shows 12%; ortho +7.2%, CMI +1.4%. Southeast/Texas 6.3%; Midwest/Northeast 2.1%. $250M service lines, AI scribing; guide Q4 4-5% admissions, 5-6% days.

Finally, impact of cost reduction initiatives: $285 million run-rate YTD savings, +240 bps EBITDA to 18.2%. Labor $112M: Smart Staffing AI down overtime 22%, agency 35%, RN $44.20/hour. Supply $98M: GPO bundling 18%, blockchain pharma. Op/SG&A $75M: RPA denials to 7.8%, IoT energy 16%, divestitures $145M, LOS 4.2 days. Reinvest $114M ASCs/digital; FY25 $100M more.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Michael Reynolds to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Dr. Carter. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Carter mentioned, we had an exceptionally strong quarter. Net revenue for the fourth quarter was $4.5 billion, an increase of 14% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives, and the impact of our strategic acquisitions.

Our operating expenses were $3.8 billion, representing 85% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $320 million, or $2.25 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and are raising our guidance for the full year.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Sarah Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Sarah Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning. We are making significant strides in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our CareBridge clinical program has shown remarkable results, with a 15% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, remote patient monitoring programs, and AI-powered diagnostic tools like FluSmart and ValueSync.

Following that, Lisa Chen will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including AI-driven scheduling from Qventus and bed orchestration platforms, which have resulted in significant cost savings, improved patient flow, and enhanced staff productivity.

Next, Robert Kline will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, Lisa. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets like the Sunbelt, enhance our service offerings through micro-hospitals and ASCs, and diversify our revenue streams via value-based contracts.

After that, David Wong will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

David Wong:
Thank you, Robert. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures to enhance our cybersecurity posture, ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, and mitigate the risk of data breaches, including air-gapping claims processing post-Change Healthcare. We are also investing in cloud-based solutions like Google Cloud for scalability and Epic integrations for interoperability.

Following that, Maria Gonzalez will discuss our efforts related to workforce development and employee engagement.

Maria Gonzalez:
Thank you, David. We are committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly skilled and engaged workforce. We are implementing several initiatives to improve employee satisfaction, enhance training and development opportunities like clinical apprenticeships, and promote a culture of diversity and inclusion, achieving 92% retention through premium pay and internal travel programs.

Finally, Thomas Lee will elaborate on our compliance efforts.

Thomas Lee:
Thank you, Maria. We are dedicated to maintaining the highest standards of ethical conduct and regulatory compliance. We have implemented a comprehensive compliance program to ensure adherence to all applicable laws and regulations, protect patient privacy under HIPAA, and prevent fraud and abuse through denial management and HAC monitoring.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Emily Carter.

Dr. Emily Carter:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Alex Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Johnson:
Good morning. Can you provide more details on the specific initiatives you are implementing to improve employee satisfaction and retention?

Maria Gonzalez:
Good morning, Alex. Absolutely. We're addressing this head-on through a multi-faceted approach. Our internal travel nurse program now covers 15% of shifts, reducing agency dependency and boosting retention by 12% with premium pay incentives tailored to high-demand Sunbelt markets like Texas and Florida. We've rolled out AI scheduling via Qventus, cutting overtime 22% and improving work-life balance. Clinical apprenticeship programs have upskilled 1,200 LPNs, creating clear career paths. Employee engagement scores are up 15% from targeted diversity training and burnout reduction via ambient AI scribing. These have lowered blended RN costs to $44.20 per hour while maintaining 92% fill rates, well above peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
What are your plans for addressing the ongoing challenges related to regulatory compliance and cybersecurity threats?

Thomas Lee:
Thanks, Sarah. Compliance and cybersecurity are top priorities. We've enhanced our program with RPA for 65% of denial workflows, dropping rates to 7.8% and ensuring MIPS scores at 95/100. On cyber, post-Change Healthcare, we've air-gapped 90% of claims processing, invested in blockchain for pharma tracking, and partnered for real-time threat detection. Our HAC PSI-90 is at 96%, avoiding penalties, and we're aligning with CMS interoperability mandates via $90 million Epic rollout. Regional audits with payers like UnitedHealthcare are managed through CDI teams querying 42% of cases.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Torres with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Torres:
Can you elaborate on the potential impact of your strategic acquisitions on your long-term growth prospects?

Robert Kline:
Good morning, Mike. Our acquisitions, like recent ASC tuck-ins, contribute significantly. They've boosted outpatient mix to 58% of EPDs, with 25% margins versus inpatient's lower rates. Combined with $400 million capex for 25 de novo ASCs and micro-hospitals in Phoenix and Dallas, we project 10-12% volume growth and 200-300 bps margin expansion by FY2025. VBC acceleration to 40% revenue with $80-90 million savings enhances moats, especially in Sunbelt with 55% MA penetration. Payback under 5 years at 15-18% IRR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Kim with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Lisa Kim:
How are you leveraging AI to improve diagnostic accuracy?

Dr. Sarah Patel:
Hi, Lisa. AI is transformative. Our ValueSync and FluSmart platforms use Epic Cosmos and Google Cloud for predictive analytics, reducing readmissions 15% and forecasting surges two weeks out. Nuance ambient scribing cuts documentation 40%, freeing clinicians; CDI AI queries 42% cases, lifting CMI 4.1% and revenue per admission 2.8%. Oncology CAR-T and stroke detection via Viz.ai speed door-to-needle 20%, while tele-ICU boosts throughput 18%. Pilots show 12% HEDIS improvements, tying to VBC bonuses.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Chen:
Can you provide more color on Q1 seasonality expectations and capex phasing?

Michael Reynolds:
Sure, David. Q1 mirrors Q4 with CDC moderate flu but El Niño risks; we expect similar 8-12% volume surges managed via virtual care diverting 15% ED cases. Capex Q1 at $210-230 million focuses IT go-lives and equipment; peaks Q2/Q3 construction. Fully funded, targeting 15% IRR.

Dr. Emily Carter:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

John Smith:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Partners Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
